key_takeaways: Health spending reached 10.1 percent of GDP in 2024, from 9.2 percent in 2012.{{health_system.financing:1}}
International graduates were 43.5 percent of registered doctors in 2025, but only 40 percent stay two years.{{health_system.workforce:1}}
In 2024/25, 34.2 percent of adults were obese and 14.3 percent reported high or very high psychological distress.{{country_overview.disease_prevalence:6}}
In 2026 Health New Zealand signed its first long-term private hospital contracts, worth about $300 million (US$170 million).{{health_system.private_system:7}}
health_system: Health New Zealand replaced the district health boards in 2022 and delivers tax-funded universal care nationally.{{health_system.public_system:1}}
Elective treatment within four months reached 72.6 percent in 2025/26, up from 63.9 percent.{{health_system.public_system:6}}
In 2024/25, cost stopped 14.9 percent of adults visiting a GP, and 25.5 percent cited appointment waits.{{health_system.public_system:4}}
market: About 37 percent of people hold private insurance, and Southern Cross has about 60 percent of the market.{{health_system.private_system:1}}{{health_system.private_system:2}}
Icon Oncology Group runs Wellington's Bowen Icon Cancer Centre with Australian-owned Evolution Healthcare.{{health_system.competitive_landscape:1}}{{health_system.competitive_landscape:2}}
Health New Zealand signed a digital and AI innovation agreement with London's UCLPartners in July 2026.{{health_system.competitive_landscape:9}}
risks: A general election is due on 7 November 2026.{{health_system.outlook:7}} Its result will shape private outsourcing of elective surgery.
The Treasury expects superannuation and finance costs to take about 28 percent of tax revenue by 2030/31.{{country_overview.economy:4}}
Practicing nurses fell 4 percent to 80,960 at 30 June 2026, and 43.5 percent qualified overseas.{{health_system.workforce:6}}

recent.text: Mark Darrow became Health New Zealand board chair on 1 May 2026 for three years, replacing Lester Levy.{{recent_developments.2:1}}
Budget 2026 added more than $5.8 billion (US$3.29 billion) in new health operating funding, including a $1.37 billion (US$778 million) annual uplift.{{recent_developments.1:1}}
Health New Zealand reported 87.0 percent of cancer patients treated within 31 days of the treatment decision in 2025/26.{{recent_developments.0:1}}

country_background: New Zealand, a constitutional monarchy with its capital in Wellington, had about 5.36 million people at 30 June 2026 (provisional).{{country_overview.demographics:16}}{{country_overview.demographics:8}}{{country_overview.demographics:1}} Governor-General Dame Cindy Kiro represents the King, and Prime Minister Christopher Luxon leads a National, ACT and New Zealand First government.{{country_overview.government:1}}{{country_overview.government:4}} Simeon Brown is Minister of Health, and Health New Zealand has delivered public services nationally since 2022.{{country_overview.government:5}}{{country_overview.government:6}} The high-income economy grew 1.7 percent in the year ended June 2026, and GDP per person was about 57,350 international dollars (PPP) in 2025.{{country_overview.economy:3}}{{country_overview.economy:2}} The population is aging: 17.6 percent were 65 or older in 2025, and life expectancy was 82.0 years in 2024.{{country_overview.demographics:4}}{{country_overview.demographics:6}} The key risk is fiscal, because the Treasury warns that demographic change, unless checked, will make the long-term fiscal position unsustainable.{{country_overview.economy:4}}
